title: The Four Seasons in a Single Day (PT)
summary: Akbar asks Birbal whether a mortal can experience Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter in twelve hours. Birbal illustrates the seasons of human emotion. [PT]
full_text:
During a philosophical discussion on the terrace of Fatehpur Sikri, Emperor Akbar remarked: 'How wonderful nature is, taking twelve months to cycle through the freshness of Spring, the heat of Summer, the harvest of Autumn, and the chill of Winter! How tragic that human life cannot experience all four seasons in a single day!'

Birbal bowed: 'Sire, every human being experiences all four seasons in a single day, if he only observes the weather of his own heart.'

Akbar challenged him: 'Demonstrate this to me today, Birbal!'

Birbal took Akbar on a quiet stroll through the imperial city, observing citizens from morning till night.

At dawn, they visited the maternity pavilion of the public hospital. A young mother held her newborn son, her face glowing with tender joy, surrounded by blossoming marigolds:

'Sire,' Birbal whispered, 'this is the Spring of the human soul. Life is newborn, fragrant, innocent, and full of fresh hope.'

At noon, they observed a crowded blacksmiths' workshop where muscled men hammered glowing red iron anvils under a blistering sun, shouting and arguing over supplies:

'Here is the Summer of the soul, Sire. Passion, intense labor, heat, sweat, and burning ambitions that test human endurance.'

At sunset, they visited a bustling village threshing yard where old farmers laughed, sharing sweet jaggery cakes while stacking golden sheaves of wheat:

'Here is the Autumn of the soul. The harvest of labor, the contentment of achievement, and the quiet satisfaction of shared abundance.'

Finally, at midnight, they entered a quiet room where an elderly, white-bearded scholar sat in deep, silent meditation beneath a solitary oil lamp, completely detached from worldly desires:

'And here is the Winter of the soul, Sire. The outer world is cold and dark, but within, the mind has settled into peaceful stillness, preparing for the great dawn of eternity.'

Akbar stood in silent wonder, embracing Birbal for revealing that the great universe of nature is replicated entirely within the human soul.
